sentences.n: der Vortritt is the right of going first, a matter of rank — and the clerk yields it to the parson with great correctness, at the door of a sack. nachfolgen, to follow after, sets its nach at the end. Herr Pfarrer is how a parish priest is addressed.

sentences.t: Der Pfarrer schritt also vor und stieg auf die Kanzel, wo der Meister den Sack öffnete.
sentences.l: The parson strode therefore forward and climbed up into the pulpit, where the master opened the sack.
sentences.i: So the parson stepped forward and climbed up into the pulpit, where the master opened the sack.
sentences.n: also is therefore, so — never the English also. vorschreiten, to stride forward, leaves vor at the end. The whole solemn order of precedence is kept up to the last moment.

sentences.t: Der Pfarrer kroch zuerst hinein, dann der Küster.
sentences.l: The parson crawled in first, then the sexton.
sentences.i: The parson crawled in first, then the clerk.
sentences.n: hineinkriechen, to crawl in, with hinein at the end; the second clause leaves the verb out altogether, since it is the same one again. kroch is the past of kriechen.

sentences.t: Gleich band der Meister den Sack fest zu, packte ihn am Bausch und schleifte ihn die Kanzeltreppe hinab:
sentences.l: At once the master bound the sack tight shut, seized it by the bulge and dragged it down the pulpit stairs:
sentences.i: At once the master tied the sack up tight, took it by the bulge and dragged it down the pulpit stairs:
sentences.n: gleich here is at once, straight away. zubinden, to tie shut, with fest added for good measure and both standing at the end. der Bausch is the swelling part of a full sack, what one gets a grip on. schleifen is to drag along the ground.

sentences.t: so oft die Köpfe der beiden Thoren auf die Stufen aufschlugen, rief er „jetzt gehts schon über die Berge.“
sentences.l: as often as the heads of the two fools struck on the steps, he cried “now it is going over the mountains already.”
sentences.i: each time the heads of the two fools banged on the steps, he called out, “Now we are going over the mountains.”
sentences.n: der Thor is a fool, and Thoren here is its plural — the same spelling is das Thor, a gate, elsewhere in these tales, and this is not that word. aufschlagen is to strike against something. gehts is geht es, and “es geht über die Berge” is impersonal: the journey is going over the mountains.

sentences.t: Dann zog er sie auf gleiche Weise durch das Dorf, und wenn sie durch Pfützen kamen, rief er „jetzt gehts schon durch die nassen Wolken,“
sentences.l: Then he pulled them in the same way through the village, and when they came through puddles, he cried “now it is going through the wet clouds already,”
sentences.i: Then he hauled them through the village in the same manner, and when they came through puddles he called out, “Now we are going through the wet clouds,”
sentences.n: “auf gleiche Weise” is in the same manner. die Pfütze is a puddle in a village street; die Wolke a cloud. The commentary keeps pace with the bumping, and the two in the sack take every jolt for a stage of the ascent.

sentences.t: und als er sie endlich die Schloßtreppe hinaufzog, so rief er „jetzt sind wir auf der Himmelstreppe und werden bald im Vorhof sein.“
sentences.l: and when he at last pulled them up the castle stairs, then he cried “now we are on the stairway of heaven and shall soon be in the forecourt.”
sentences.i: and when he hauled them up the castle stairs at last, he called out, “Now we are on the stairway of heaven, and shall soon be in the forecourt.”
sentences.n: hinaufziehen, to pull up, with hinauf at the end. der Vorhof is the outer court of a great house, and of the Temple in the Bible — the last stage before the presence itself. die Himmelstreppe is another compound built on the spot, like Himmelsthüre.

sentences.t: Als er oben angelangt war, schob er den Sack in den Taubenschlag, und als die Tauben flatterten, sagte er „hört ihr wie die Engel sich freuen und mit den Fittichen schlagen.“
sentences.l: When he had arrived at the top, he shoved the sack into the dovecote, and when the doves fluttered, he said “do you hear how the angels are rejoicing and beating with their pinions.”
sentences.i: When he had got to the top, he shoved the sack into the dovecote; and when the doves fluttered, he said, “Do you hear how the angels rejoice and beat their wings.”
sentences.n: der Taubenschlag is a dovecote, the loft where doves are kept. der Fittich is the elevated, biblical word for a wing. “sich freuen” is to rejoice, reflexive in German. anlangen, to arrive, leaves an at the end.

sentences.t: Dann schob er den Riegel vor und gieng fort.
sentences.l: Then he shoved the bolt across and went away.
sentences.i: Then he shot the bolt and went off.
sentences.n: vorschieben, to push across, is what one does to a bolt: den Riegel vorschieben, to bolt a door. gieng is the 1857 spelling of ging, and fortgehen leaves its fort at the end.

sentences.t: Am andern Morgen begab er sich zu dem Grafen, und sagte ihm daß er auch die dritte Aufgabe gelöst und den Pfarrer und Küster aus der Kirche weggeführt hätte.
sentences.l: On the next morning he betook himself to the count, and told him that he had solved the third task too and led the parson and the sexton away out of the church.
sentences.i: The next morning he went to the count and told him that he had carried out the third task as well, and had carried the parson and the clerk off out of the church.
sentences.n: gelöst hätte and weggeführt hätte are subjunctive because the whole report is in reported speech — German marks it this way instead of leaning on the tense. wegführen is to lead away, and the auxiliary hätte is written only once, for both participles.

sentences.t: „Wo hast du sie gelassen?“ fragte der Herr.
sentences.l: “Where have you left them?” asked the lord.
sentences.i: “Where have you put them?” asked the lord.
sentences.n: lassen here is to leave a thing somewhere — “wo hast du es gelassen?” is where have you left it. der Herr is the count in his character as master, the word the tale has used for him from the first page.

sentences.t: „Sie liegen in einem Sack oben auf dem Taubenschlag und bilden sich ein sie wären im Himmel.“
sentences.l: “They are lying in a sack up on the dovecote and imagine to themselves they are in heaven.”
sentences.i: “They are lying in a sack up on the dovecote, imagining they are in heaven.”
sentences.n: “sich etwas einbilden” is to imagine a thing about oneself, to fancy it, and its ein stands at the end. wären is subjunctive: it is what they suppose, not what is.

sentences.t: Der Graf stieg selbst hinauf und überzeugte sich daß er die Wahrheit gesagt hatte.
sentences.l: The count climbed up himself and convinced himself that he had told the truth.
sentences.i: The count climbed up himself and satisfied himself that the man had told the truth.
sentences.n: “sich überzeugen” is to convince oneself, to make sure. hinaufsteigen leaves hinauf at the end. German has one er for both men here, and the sense has to settle which is which — it is the thief who told the truth.

sentences.t: Als er den Pfarrer und Küster aus dem Gefängnis befreit hatte, sprach er „du bist ein Erzdieb, und hast deine Sache gewonnen.
sentences.l: When he had freed the parson and the sexton from the prison, he spoke “you are an arch-thief, and have won your cause.
sentences.i: When he had freed the parson and the clerk from their prison, he said, “You are an arch-thief, and you have won your case.
sentences.n: das Gefängnis, the prison, is the dovecote — the tale says it flatly, without a smile. der Erzdieb is built with the prefix Erz-, arch-, as in Erzbischof, archbishop; it outranks even Meisterdieb. “seine Sache gewinnen” is to win one’s case, as at law.

sentences.t: Für diesmal kommst du mit heiler Haut davon, aber mache daß du aus meinem Land fortkommst, denn wenn du dich wieder darin betreten läßt, so kannst du auf deine Erhöhung am Galgen rechnen.“
sentences.l: For this time you get off with a whole skin, but see that you get out of my land, for if you let yourself be caught in it again, then you can count on your elevation at the gallows.”
sentences.i: This time you get off with a whole skin; but see that you get out of my country, for if you let yourself be found in it again, you may count on being raised up on the gallows.”
sentences.n: “mit heiler Haut davonkommen” is to get off unhurt. “mache daß du fortkommst” is a brisk see that you clear off. “sich betreten lassen” is an old turn: to let oneself be come upon, be caught. die Erhöhung is a raising up, and normally a promotion — the count means the hanging, and the joke is his last word on the whole business.

sentences.t: Der Erzdieb nahm Abschied von seinen Eltern, gieng wieder in die weite Welt, und niemand hat wieder etwas von ihm gehört.
sentences.l: The arch-thief took leave of his parents, went again into the wide world, and nobody has heard anything of him again.
sentences.i: The arch-thief took his leave of his parents, went off again into the wide world, and nobody has ever heard anything of him since.
sentences.n: “Abschied nehmen von” is to take one’s leave of somebody. The last line answers the father’s words on the first page — “seitdem habe ich nichts von ihm gehört” — with the same phrase, and the tale closes where it opened, with the son gone and no news of him.

glossary.abschied: der Abschied — leave, farewell (Abschied nehmen von, to take one’s leave of)
glossary.altem: alt — old (dat. sg. of the strong adjective: mit altem Wein)
glossary.alter: alt — old (masc. nom.; ein alter Mann)
glossary.anfangen: anfangen — to do with, to make of (was soll er damit anfangen, what is he to do with it); by itself, to begin
glossary.arme: der Arm — arms (pl.; auf die Arme nehmen, to take into one’s arms). The same spelling is also arm, poor, inflected — both occur in this tale
glossary.armen: arm — poor (adj., inflected; der arme Sünder, the condemned criminal)
glossary.band: binden — tied, bound (3rd sg. preterite; here festbinden and zubinden, particle at the end)

glossary.dinge: das Ding — things (gen. pl.; das Ende aller Dinge, the end of all things)
glossary.erheben: erheben — to raise (infinitive; ein Geschrei erheben, to set up a cry)
glossary.es: es — it (neuter pronoun; also the impersonal es of es gibt, es geht)
glossary.euerm: euer — your (dat. sg.; 1857 form of eurem, with the plural address ihr)
glossary.fest: fest — firm, tight, fast (adj./adv.; fest halten, festbinden, with fest standing at the end of the clause)
glossary.folge: nachfolgen — I follow after (1st sg.; folge … nach)
glossary.gelöst: lösen — solved, carried out (past part.; die Aufgabe gelöst)
glossary.gericht: das Gericht — a dish, a prepared course of food (the same word also means a court of law)
glossary.gescheidter: gescheidt — clever, shrewd (adj., masc. nom.; 1857 spelling of gescheit)
glossary.gezogen: ziehen — trained, brought up (past part.; of a tree or a child)
glossary.glaubt: glauben — believe, think (imperative pl.; glaubt nicht, do not think)
glossary.hals: der Hals — neck (es geht dir an den Hals, it is a matter of your life)
glossary.herzog: der Herzog — duke (noun; not the past tense of herziehen, which is spelt the same)
glossary.hexen: hexen — to practise witchcraft (infinitive; from die Hexe, a witch)
glossary.hört: hören — hear (imperative pl. in hört an, give ear; also 2nd pl., hört ihr, do you hear)
glossary.jüngste: jüngst — last, latest (der jüngste Tag, the Last Day, the Day of Judgement)
glossary.jüngsten: jüngst — last, latest (gen. sg.; des jüngsten Tags, of the Day of Judgement)
glossary.kanzel: die Kanzel — pulpit, the raised desk a sermon is preached from
glossary.kette: die Kette — chain (the chain a horse is tethered by)
glossary.klebte: kleben — stuck, glued (3rd sg. preterite; klebte … auf and klebte … an, the particle at the end)
glossary.knorzig: knorzig — gnarled, knotty (adj.; said here of a man grown hard with age)
glossary.knüpfte: festknüpfen — knotted fast, tied on (3rd sg. preterite; knüpfte … fest)
glossary.krieche: kriechen — let him crawl (3rd sg. subjunctive used as a command)
glossary.lauerte: lauern — lay in wait (3rd sg. preterite)
glossary.leichte: leicht — easy, light (adj., inflected; auf eine leichte Art, by an easy road)
glossary.los: los — loose, free (losbinden, to untie; loslassen, to let go; losdrücken, to pull the trigger)
glossary.lösen: lösen — to solve, to carry out (eine Aufgabe lösen, to carry out a set task)
